text: This lesson covers T D D B D D
A T D D exploratory testing and core test
design techniques We use a discount and checkout feature
as our example Begin with a checkout rule an
eligible member receives a ten-percent discount but an expired
coupon must be rejected There are several questions hidden
inside that sentence We need to clarify eligibility calculate
the amount investigate limits and observe the user journey
T D D B D D A T D
D and exploratory testing can help but they work
at different points and with different intentions Test design
techniques help choose examples systematically The objective is not
to use every method on every story It is
to choose methods that give useful evidence about the
most important risks
Write a failing test for an eligible ten-percent discount
implement enough code to pass then refactor safely The
Red Green Refactor loop encourages small verified changes For
a T D D demonstration write a small test
saying that a purchase of one thousand rupees produces
a one-hundred-rupee discount for an eligible member Confirm the
test fails because the function has not implemented that
behavior Add the smallest implementation that makes it pass
Refactor the design while keeping the test green Next
add an ineligible-customer case expecting zero These examples should
guide the code in small steps Writing all production
code first and adding tests afterward can still be
useful but it does not provide the same design
feedback loop as test-driven development
Describe behavior collaboratively using Given When and Then Given
an eligible coupon when it is applied to a
qualifying order then the specified discount is calculated B
D D is about shared understanding not just automation
syntax For B D D gather product development and
testing perspectives before choosing automation syntax Ask how a
customer knows that a coupon was accepted and how
the final total should change Express an example given
an eligible member with a qualifying basket when a
valid coupon is applied then the agreed discount appears
and the total is updated Now discuss an expired
coupon and a basket below the minimum Given When
and Then can make examples readable but the format
is not the purpose The purpose is a shared
understanding of observable behavior including situations where assumptions differ
Define acceptance examples with business development and testing participants
before implementation For refunds clarify eligible and ineligible cases
timing and expected outcomes A T D D and
B D D overlap but are not identical A
T D D also brings acceptance examples forward For
a refund feature agree that an eligible cancelled purchase
returns the correct amount and changes the order state
Include an ineligible refund a partial refund and a
delayed provider confirmation if those apply to the product
The team can use these examples to guide implementation
and later verification B D D and A T
D D overlap in collaborative discovery and examples their
labels do not define a rigid boundary for every
team What matters is that acceptance expectations are clear
before code is judged complete and that the checks
reflect real business outcomes
Investigate checkout by changing quantities applying coupons and navigating
backward Adapt based on observations Use charters notes and
debriefs to keep exploration purposeful Exploratory testing adds responsive
investigation Set a charter investigate whether coupon changes can
leave checkout totals inconsistent Begin with a normal purchase
change quantity apply a coupon navigate backward and return
Observe what changes and follow surprising behavior Record the
data actions and findings so another person can understand
the investigation A timebox helps focus the session but
curiosity should still respond to evidence Exploration is not
random clicking It combines learning test design and execution
while the tester updates the next question based on
what the product actually does
Equivalence partitioning groups inputs with similar behavior Boundary analysis
checks values around limits Decision tables cover combinations of
rules such as membership and coupon eligibility Use equivalence
partitioning and boundaries for a coupon that accepts whole-number
quantities from one through ten Valid quantities form one
partition zero and negative values are invalid values above
ten are invalid Representative examples can reduce redundant checks
Boundary analysis gives special attention to zero one ten
and eleven Other values may be needed depending on
the input type and risks If the input permits
decimals or text those introduce additional partitions The specification
must define the expected result A technique helps choose
inputs but it cannot resolve an unclear rule about
whether a particular input is allowed
Use T D D for calculations B D D
for shared renewal behavior A T D D for
refund acceptance boundary tests for limits and exploration for
user journeys Select methods based on risk Build a
decision table for two conditions the customer is a
member and the coupon is valid There are four
combinations Agree on the outcome for a member with
a valid coupon a member with an invalid coupon
a nonmember with a valid coupon and a nonmember
with an invalid coupon Maybe membership is required or
maybe the coupon is available to anyone the product
rule decides A table makes missing combinations visible Add
columns only when they affect the decision because many
independent conditions can produce more combinations than a team
can practically test through the interface
For your exercise design checks for a discount feature
with a minimum spend of five hundred rupees State
whether the threshold is inclusive then choose values immediately
below at and above it Add an expired coupon
example and one combination of membership and eligibility Finally
write a short exploratory charter about changing the basket
after applying a coupon Explain which method supports each
part Boundary analysis addresses the threshold shared examples clarify
behavior and exploration investigates interactions The strongest plan combines
these views while avoiding multiple expensive checks that all
prove the same narrow rule
Work through a boundary example numerically The fictional coupon
applies when the qualifying subtotal is at least five
hundred rupees Test four hundred and ninety-nine five hundred
and five hundred and one when the rule operates
on whole rupees If the application supports paise values
immediately around the boundary need that finer precision instead
Confirm whether the subtotal is calculated before or after
other discounts and whether tax contributes Without those decisions
two tests with the same apparent basket value may
legitimately expect different results Boundary analysis is effective only
when the unit precision and rule being bounded are
explicit
Add an interaction example A customer applies a coupon
to a qualifying basket then removes an item so
the basket falls below the minimum The total should
be recalculated according to the agreed rule and the
customer should understand the change A focused rule check
can verify the arithmetic while a browser journey can
verify the integration and message An exploratory session can
investigate other sequences such as changing quantity while a
request is still pending Avoid writing every variation as
a slow end-to-end test automatically Choose the least expensive
layer that provides useful evidence and retain a smaller
set of integrated journeys for risks that depend on
interactions
Different techniques answer different quality questions Knowledge check which
technique targets values immediately above and below an allowed
limit Subscribe to Tech at sixty for the next
episode in this Agile Testing Masterclass Practice the example
with synthetic data and share the most important risk
you identified in the comments
